design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (claim_repair_billing_desk, M=2). Draw: `draw_counts.py <diff> --task 1` -> {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 6]}; root claim_ext_overpayment_refund and prerequisite claim_ext_denied_operation_price take 6 factors each.
SCOPE SNAPSHOT. Occupied by task 0: claim_ext_unrelated_addition_price (sign_unrelated_damage_addition_ef94c675) and claim_ext_authorization_repair_days (record_insurer_authorization_cee3bb86). Claimed here: the customer's acceptance of operations the insurer refused on a supplement (denied_operation additions, accept_denied_operations_addition_a285270b, user) and the overpayment refund (claim_customer_refund, issue_overpayment_refund_b142d0d2, agent). The denied-operation price is a separate business decision from task 0's unrelated-damage price: it is driven by the insurer's partial decision on a supplement and the calibration order it touched, not by a scope card. No policy or tool is left unclaimed; the two tasks are disjoint and cover all four extended policies.
WHY A GOOD TEST. The customer asks only for his overpayment back. The policy forbids refunding while a customer-pay addition form awaits the customer, and the denied-operation form for the partly refused Multi-System calibration is pending; the agent must price it (six factors over the supplement, the calibration order, its alignment checks, the warranty and the repair start date), hand the signature to the customer, and then compute a refund net of that signed work and of five holds, capped by the right payment. Refunding immediately returns 1181.70; reading only the computation documents gives 957.40 for the form and 120.00 for the refund; gold is 936.20 and 245.50.
DEPTH AND BREADTH. Hop 1: refund rule -> prerequisite sentence 'An overpayment is not refunded until every customer-pay addition consent issued on the repair order stands signed or revoked.' -> form cb56630d-bc58-40ab-834a-168779b68ddc pending_customer -> the denied-operation price policy is the only write that turns it signed ('The customer signs the customer-pay addition consent for operations the insurer denied at the price this rule gives'). Hop 2: price it from supplement #1 and the Multi-System order. Hop 3: refund with the signed work netted. Reads span claim_repairs, claim_ledger (10 rows), claim_consents, claim_supplements (3 rows), adas_orders (2), adas_events, adas_ledger, warranty_coverages, warranty_ledger, estimate_bookings, estimate_events, carrier_agreements, vehicles.
FACTOR CARD - claim_ext_denied_operation_price (result 936.20, all-baseline 957.40). insurer_calibration_allowance (method): supplement #1 1a02b6c0-c982-45a4-8722-036bf56d1737 partly approved 398.36; kept labor 0.4 h x 123.40 = 49.36; allowance 349.00; line 546.00 (baseline 1250.30). denied_work_hourly_rate (parameter): calibrations, no structural -> 115.00 (baseline 925.20). minimum_billable_hours (method): 0.6 h -> 1.0 h (baseline 890.20). customer_alignment_checks (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty adas): checks 502b28bb-e17d-40d6-9c38-4e166ea66e13 (out of spec, corrected) and e5ccb1a1-313b-4bf1-885a-5f8d6f720956 (in spec) on order b1938f3a-651f-439a-a434-729f799cf2f0 -> 249.85 (baseline 686.35); near-miss: the second check was not corrected, so only one correction fee applies. calibration_warranty_discount (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty warranty): warranty 715e90ab-077f-4554-90e8-e66bdd6fb9ae issued 2026-02-18, 7 months -> 10 percent (baseline 990.80); near-miss: the earlier Dynamic Camera order 5aa05d3c-dd68-4e29-b098-977d3eedfb9c is not the repair's calibration order and must not set the tier price. pre_calibration_scan (parameter): 15 days since 2026-09-29 -> 79.95 (baseline 856.25).
FACTOR CARD - claim_ext_overpayment_refund (result 245.50, all-baseline 120.00). refunded_payment_choice (method): card 8a3df7a4-c808-44e0-82ff-b6245edc9024 1600.00 on 2026-10-09 within 120 days -> cap 1600.00 (baseline latest payment, check 120.00 -> 120.00); near-miss: the 780.00 card payment is older and is not the most recent card payment. reinspection_reserve (parameter): supplement #2 101b2df4-6de7-49b0-933c-7aa0a17e63e8 undecided on field reinspection -> 50.00 (baseline 295.50). deductible_exposure_hold (parameter, multi-source): unassessed 2500.00 - 1178.36 = 1321.64 >= 286.50 -> 286.50 (baseline 532.00). betterment_exposure_hold (parameter): 42.80 expected on #2 (baseline 288.30). funds_clearing_hold (parameter): check b703998c-ace5-4163-85cb-d844cb9a72b5 2 days old -> 120.00 (baseline 365.50); near-miss: the ACH of 2026-10-08 is 6 days old, past the 5 return days, so it is not held. other_desk_charges_hold (parameter, cross-difficulty estimate): mobile trip charge a5b1a963-dff9-438c-9296-80ddf343fd74 39.00 unpaid -> 39.00 (baseline 284.50).
BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Refund (subject claim_customer_refund): claim_evt_customer_payments gate refund_names_payment - the refund names payment 8a3df7a4-c808-44e0-82ff-b6245edc9024, which has no refund yet (no claim_customer_refund row cites it); the refund goes to that payment's method (card); the declared override replaces the base refund-amount sentence with the netted and held refund. Signature (subject claim_customer_charge): deductible_betterment and withdrawal have no gate on this subject; customer_pay_additions' consent gate and storage's free-day gate are retired by the declared overrides; the unrelated-work allowance counts unrelated-damage consents only, and the order carries none, so it is untouched. No time gate remains on either write.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target repair order 31b11a88-b22f-47a6-bcb8-f259cd9d3947 (Accord, claim EFI-PA-26-0917-24816, on hold). Price object: the single pending denied-operation form cb56630d-bc58-40ab-834a-168779b68ddc; its supplement is the most recently decided one, #1. Refund object: the 1600.00 card payment; included in the excess: all four customer payments and both deductible charges; no credits or refunds exist. Calibration order b1938f3a-651f-439a-a434-729f799cf2f0 names the repair order; the old order 5aa05d3c-dd68-4e29-b098-977d3eedfb9c (customer request) carries its own paid charge and is the warranty source. Estimate booking 4c68f384-65be-453e-b245-26c9fb483b9e (customer-pay Mobile Estimate, cancelled late) carries the unpaid 39.00 trip charge; the converted Drive-In booking 0a41e774-195e-4d48-89f0-dfac4360baa9 carries no charge.
SEED ROWS AND WHY. Supplements give the allowance, the hourly rate, the reserve, the deductible exposure and the betterment hold; ledger rows give the excess, the deductible assessed, the payment choice and the clearing hold; the pending form is the prerequisite; adas rows give the tier price, the alignment charges and the diagnostic fee; the warranty gives the discount; the mobile booking's charge gives the other-desk hold; the carrier agreement explains the field reinspection routes. Automatic clauses checked: no storage (not complete), no betterment charge owed (no betterment applied on #1), deductible top-up for #1 posted, supplement #2 undecided (insurer late), so nothing else is owed by the desk.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root claim_ext_overpayment_refund <- prerequisite claim_ext_denied_operation_price; value_input, gate r_committed, form state, sentence 'An overpayment is not refunded until every customer-pay addition consent issued on the repair order stands signed or revoked.' (negated direction 'not ... until', record-visible state, no tool/id/code token; the business states a refund as not made until what it waits for stands, while task 0 states a planned figure as fixed only after its state - the charter carries both directions). False at frozen_time: initial_state.claim_consents.cb56630d-bc58-40ab-834a-168779b68ddc.consent_status = pending_customer. Only the customer's acceptance tool turns a pending denied-operation form signed. Deletion sensitivity: without it the refund is 1181.70 (vs 245.50). Order: signature then refund; single edge.
PERSONA DESIGN. Gerald Hutchins, retired HVAC technician, methodical. Volunteered: his payments as he remembers them (780 card, 398.36 ACH, 1,600 card on Oct 9, 120 check on Oct 12; all match the ledger) and the request to refund the overpayment, preferably to his card. On request: name, phone 7175550268, PIN 2483, ZIP, email, claim number. Passive: if the agent raises the calibration form he wants the full calibration done and will pay the uncovered part; he signs with the reference and price given; he accepts that some money stays on the order; on hearing the refund amount he repeats it and ends. Neither 936.20 nor 245.50 appears.
STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers -> verify(phone, PIN) -> find_vehicles -> find_claim_repairs -> find_claim_ledger -> find_claim_consents -> find_claim_supplements -> find_adas_orders -> find_adas_events -> find_adas_ledger -> find_warranty_coverages -> unlock + customer call accept_denied_operations_addition_a285270b(cb56630d-bc58-40ab-834a-168779b68ddc, 936.20) -> find_carrier_agreements -> find_estimate_bookings -> find_estimate_events -> find_warranty_ledger -> unlock + call issue_overpayment_refund_b142d0d2(repair order, 8a3df7a4-c808-44e0-82ff-b6245edc9024, 245.50).
VERIFICATION. Authoring evaluator (check_compute.build_env/eval_compute): price 936.20 (sens 1250.30/925.20/890.20/686.35/990.80/856.25, all-baseline 957.40); refund 245.50 on the post-signature world (sens 120.00/295.50/532.00/288.30/365.50/284.50, all-baseline 120.00; pre-signature 1181.70). Gates with --task 1: EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK (19 actions, closure 31 = initial 31); SOLVABILITY OK; COMPUTE OK (factors 12, cross 3); GROUNDING OK; SCOPE OK.
CLOSURE. claim_ext_denied_operation_price -> accept_denied_operations_addition_a285270b -> amount_usd 936.20 at the user call; claim_ext_overpayment_refund -> issue_overpayment_refund_b142d0d2 -> amount_usd 245.50 against source_entry_id 8a3df7a4-c808-44e0-82ff-b6245edc9024 at the agent call. Scope, required documents and first-call tool order match.
DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the published rules and lookups alone: the refund rule's prerequisite sentence and the pending form force the signature first; the price rule over supplement #1, the Multi-System tier (895.00, alignment fees 59.95/129.95, diagnostic 79.95), two alignment checks, the warranty date and the start date gives 936.20; the refund rule then gives min(1600.00, 1720.00 - 936.20 - 50.00 - 286.50 - 42.80 - 120.00 - 39.00) = 245.50 against the October 9 card payment. Agrees with gold.
REVISIONS. (1) An earlier draft read 'is not' in compute; the restricted grammar rejects it -> rewritten with '!= None'. (2) The undecided supplement was first found by subtracting submitted totals of decided supplements, which over-counts with several decisions -> replaced by comparing the latest submitted and latest decided supplement numbers. (3) The old calibration order needed its paid charge seeded so the warranty source reads as finished work; find_adas_ledger added to the reads.
REWORK ROUND 2 (policy-task audit; this task passed and its scored values are unchanged: 936.20 and 245.50). T1-O5: refunded_payment_choice is no longer labelled multi-source in factor_trace or the factor card (its tiers read the payment rows only); the task's multi-source factor is deductible_exposure_hold. T1-O6: the statement that the 0.6 denied hours sit within the unrelated-work allowance was removed - that allowance counts unrelated-damage consents only. O-4: the refund edge's effect text in the charter is now phrased for any pending customer-pay consent. Charter changes made for task 0's findings (scan-credit wording, scope-rate tier, daily-hours ladder, hidden-damage method) touch no policy of this task.
user_scenario: You are Gerald Hutchins, a retired HVAC technician from Harrisburg, Pennsylvania: patient, methodical, and you like to have your papers in front of you. Your 2021 Honda Accord EX is in for a collision repair at Crestline's Harrisburg center under your own collision coverage with Evergreen Fidelity Insurance Company, and your policy carries a 2,500-dollar deductible. You paid 780 dollars by card when you dropped the car off and 398.36 dollars by bank transfer after the first supplement, as the statements asked. Then on October 9 you put 1,600 dollars on your card through the online payment page because you thought the rest of your deductible was due right away, and on October 12 you mailed a 120-dollar check after a reminder letter you now think crossed in the mail. You realise you have paid far more than the repair order shows you owe, and you are calling to have the overpayment refunded to you, preferably back to your card. You want the desk to issue the refund now; you are not asking to cancel the repair, change insurers or talk to anyone else. You open by explaining that you overpaid on your repair and would like the extra refunded. You give details only when asked: your name is Gerald Hutchins, the phone number on your account is 717-555-0268 (7175550268 as digits), your account PIN is 2483, your ZIP code is 17112 and your email is gerald.hutchins@gmail.com. If asked for the claim number you read it from your insurer's letter: EFI-PA-26-0917-24816. You do not know any internal reference numbers. Only if the agent brings up the form for the calibration work your insurer did not fully approve do you talk about it: you tell the agent you want the camera and radar work done properly, so you want them to have the full calibration done and you will pay the part the insurer would not cover; you do not want to leave it out. You have no idea of the exact figure and you do not argue with the price the agent works out; if it sounds high you only ask the agent to check it again against your records, and you accept the figure the agent confirms. When the agent hands you the step to sign that form yourself, you run it with the reference number and the price the agent gives you, and you tell the agent once it shows as signed. If the agent explains that part of your money stays on the repair order for now, you accept that without arguing. Once the agent tells you the amount being refunded and where it is going, you repeat the amount back, thank the agent and end the call.
